summary: Reviewed all 24 listed files. Core PlutusCore/UPLC files (CekMachine, CekValue, Term/, FlatEncoding, TextEncoding, PreProcess, ScriptEncoding) contain formal mathematical content: inductive type definitions (Frame, Stack, State, EvaluationResult, CekValue, Term, Const, BuiltinFun, Version, Program), typeclass instances (BEq, LT, Repr, ToExpr), parser/decoder specifications with formal specs (FlatEncoding decoder matching spec sections C.1–C.6, TextEncoding parser matching grammar), and theorems with proofs (CekMachine/Lemmas.lean: runSteps_halt, runSteps_succ, runSteps_add, runSteps_halt_iff_stepN, cekExecuteProgram_halt_stable; FlatEncoding/Tests.lean and ScriptEncoding/Tests.lean with native_decide proofs; PreProcess/Tests.lean with rfl proofs; ConformanceUtils with programsEvalEquiv, budgetMatches). The Benchmark/PrepUplc/Driver files (Cases, Main, Report, Runner), Harness, Inputs, GenConformanceTests, lakefile, and import barrels (Benchmark.lean, Tests/Basic.lean) are engineering/tooling infrastructure with no mathematical theorems/proofs. However, the prior review RRV-fc23eabae7c3-r2 explicitly retained the conformance generator, lakefile, and import barrels. Per FILTER-002 (high evidence bar for hard exclusion), FILTER-004 (requires prover-aware check), FILTER-021 (no recall optimization), and FILTER-025 (default retain), all files stay searchable.
